effect_on_the_score.frozen_v1_first_run: 272/400 on the decided denominator. UNCHANGED and unchangeable.

errata.fix_for_v2: The generator emits 'kiloohm'; the vocabulary guard checks both sides.
errata.forge_behaviour: Correct, and the refusal is exemplary: it names the field path, quotes the string, says which dimension was wanted and gives an example. Guessing that 'kilohm' meant 'kiloohm' is the substitution the boundary exists to refuse.
errata.new_evidence: The generator spelled resistances 'kilohm'. The unit registry defines 'kiloohm' and does not define 'kilohm', so every such payload is refused with MissingUnitError naming the field, the string and the dimension expected. Verified directly: Quantity(1.0, 'kiloohm') constructs, Quantity(1.0, 'kilohm') raises.
errata.old_frozen_truth: SUPPORTED / NOT_SUPPORTED / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, per case. The oracle assessed a design whose declaration the boundary would never have accepted.
errata.why_the_oracle_failed: The challenge's vocabulary guard, assert_vocabulary_closed, checked that the ORACLE could read every unit the generator emits. Nothing checked that the RUNTIME could. A closed vocabulary on one side of a comparison is not a closed vocabulary, and the guard's own docstring -- 'a generator that grows a unit this module cannot read would fail case-by-case at truth time' -- describes only half the failure mode.

errata.fix_for_v2: The transcribed contract carries the interval bound.
errata.new_evidence: CellLimits refuses a soc_step_resolution outside [0, 1] at construction: InvalidScientificProblem, 'soc_step_resolution must lie in [0, 1]'. A resolution is a fraction of the charge axis, so the bound is definitional.
errata.why_the_oracle_failed: admissibility.battery_refusal checked soc_step_resolution for POSITIVITY and not for the unit interval. The transcription was incomplete, which is the standing risk of transcribing a contract rather than importing it -- and importing it is what would end the challenge's independence.

not_an_erratum.why: Its frozen truth -- REJECTED_AT_BOUNDARY, because a zero residence time is not a reactor -- is CORRECT. The first run recorded ERROR:ZeroDivisionError because the RUNNER divided a volume by that zero to build a flow rate before Forge was reached. The runner is not part of the freeze; the row stands in FORGE_FIRST_RUN.json because a first run is not corrected.

not_an_erratum.case: ELE00005 and the rest of the AT_BOUNDARY stratum
not_an_erratum.why: Placed on the bound to within 1e-13 relative, and the two implementations round opposite ways. That is not a defect in either; it is why the whole stratum carries ARITHMETIC_SENSITIVE and sits outside the primary denominator. It is the challenge's own prediction coming true rather than a truth being wrong.

note: Truths in benchmarks/blind/v1 that were PROVEN WRONG after Forge ran. Recorded, never edited. TRUTH.json still says what it said, its digest still matches FREEZE.json, and the v1 first-run score stands at what it scored. A corrected corpus is a NEW challenge version.
why_not_edited: The v1 number is only worth anything because nothing could move it after the run. Repairing a truth that a run disagreed with is the exact move -- NEW CASE, FORGE, ADJUST TRUTH, PASS -- that this round exists to make impossible. An erratum costs the score and keeps the method.
